title: Dynamic embed-dim proxy and online reindex signal protocol
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Summary:
We need a low-risk, production-safe approach to support embedding vector dimensionality changes (both shrinking and expansion) across our hosted/ dedicated/ private deployments. Goals: preserve client experience (no hard failures), limit reindex costs, and keep reranker quality and latency within SLOs.

Problem statement:
- Customers and open models sometimes change embedding dimensionality across model versions (e.g., 768 -> 1024 or 1024 -> 512). Existing indexes are dimension-sensitive and most third-party/vector DBs require full reindex for dim changes.
- Large-scale reindexes are expensive (IO, GPU, downtime), cause temporary quality regressions for reranking pipelines, and complicate client compatibility.
- Current clients receive 400-level errors or inconsistent results when dimension mismatches occur. SDKs lack transparent negotiation.

Proposed solution (high-level):
1) Embed-dim proxy (runtime shim): a lightweight request/response layer deployed in front of vector ingestion and query paths that:
   - Negotiates an embedding schema version via an HTTP header (X-Embed-Schema: v2; dim=1024).
   - Performs non-destructive transformations: deterministic truncation (drop highest-frequency tail) or padded projection (zero-pad or learned linear projection) for writes/reads when safe.
   - Emits metrics (embed_dim_mismatch_count, rewrite_latency_ms, projected_tokens) and tags requests for later reindex prioritization.
2) Versioned index aliasing: allow two index pointers for each namespace: active-alias (serving) and migrating-alias (bulk reindex target). Swap aliases atomically after validation.
3) Online background reindex queue: priority-based reindex worker that reindexes documents flagged by proxy; supports rate-limited parallelism and throttling by customer/region.
4) Client-facing SDK changes: graceful negotiation fallback in SDKs (JS/Python/Go): if mismatch, SDK retries with header to request server-side projection and surfaces a diagnostic code (EMB_DIM_ADJUSTED) to apps.
5) Reranker compatibility layer: when reranker model requires native dim, route through a transient projection service that yields cached projected vectors to reduce recompute.

Engineering trade-offs and decisions considered:
- Learned linear projection vs zero-padding: learned projection preserves more quality but requires training and storage for projection matrices; zero-padding is zero-cost but can degrade similarity geometry for some models. We'll pilot learned projection for high-value customers and zero-pad as safe fallback.
- On-the-fly projection overhead: adds CPU/GPU cost and latency; mitigate via caching and batching of projection operations and using quantized matrices for projection when possible.
- Reindex cadence: full immediate reindex is fastest for consistency but expensive. We propose incremental background reindexing with prioritization (recent docs and high-signal corpora first).

Acceptance criteria / success metrics:
- No client request returns embedding-dimension-mismatch 5xx/4xx errors for customers adopting negotiation header during canary.
- Reranking end-to-end P95 latency increases by <= 10% in canary.
- Reindex throughput configurable per-customer; default throttles prevent >15% extra cluster load.
- Quality: small-scale A/B eval shows learned projection preserves >= 95% of nDCG@10 compared to full reindex for top rerank workloads.

Rollout plan (phased):
Phase 0 - Design & infra spikes (2 sprints): implement proxy spec, metrics, and index aliasing support.
Phase 1 - Internal canary (1 month): enable proxy for internal tenants and our largest test customers; run projection experiments and tune matrices.
Phase 2 - Public SDK opt-in (4 weeks): release SDKs with negotiation and opt-in header; document explicit opt-in for server projection.
Phase 3 - Autoswap & bulk reindex (6 weeks): enable background reindex workers and alias atomic swaps; provide dashboard for migration status.
Phase 4 - Default behaviour (post-canary): server accepts negotiation header by default; begin deprecation schedule for clients that do not opt-in and require hard-dim compatibility.

Runbook and rollback:
- If projection-induced regressions detected (alert: rerank_quality_regression), immediately revert alias swap and pause reindex workers for affected customers.
- Emergency kill-switch: disable projection behavior cluster-wide via feature-flag; proxy will return 412 with migration guidance to client.

Open implementation tasks (next steps):
- Prototype projection service and store projection matrices in object-store with version tagging.
- Add embed_dim_mismatch_count, projection_cache_hit_rate, and reindex_queue_depth to Console dashboards.
- Add API contract docs (Confluence) and SDK PR templates.
- Create migration cost estimator that projects USD and token-hour cost for reindexing each namespace.

Links to artifacts and PRs:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Embedding+Schema+Negotiation+Spec (draft)
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/proxy/pull/487 (WIP)
- Index aliasing RFC: https://docs.redwood.ai/rfcs/2026-embed-aliasing.md

Notes:
- Coordination required with Product (reranker owners), Infra (index capacity planning), and SDK teams.
- For private deployments we will provide a configuration flag to run projection-only mode (no background reindex) to respect data residency constraints.
